data.title: Database
data.tagline: Store and find application data such as users, posts, and orders
data.description: After someone publishes a post, the backend stores it so it remains available after refresh or sign-in. CRUD names the four common operations: create, read, update, and delete. Data kept only in one browser does not automatically appear on another device.

distinctions.label: Browser storage
distinctions.explanation: A Database lets the backend store and query data centrally for many users. Browser Storage better suits device-local theme choices, offline drafts, and short-lived caches.

flowLesson.boundary: Images and large files often live in object storage, while the database keeps their URL, owner, and status. Not every persistent byte belongs in a database field.

practice.title: The backend returns success, but refresh still cannot load the data. How do you verify the database step?

options.label: Query the written record by id and owner, then confirm refresh uses the same identifier
options.feedback: Correct. The id and owner prove the record, while the refresh identifier proves the read target.

options.label: Find the newest similar record by timestamp and treat it as this save
options.feedback: Under concurrent writes, the newest record may belong to another request; verify id and ownership.

options.label: Compare the total row count before and after saving; one extra row proves the targets match
options.feedback: A row count cannot identify the record, and an update may not change the count at all.

flowLesson.agentPrompt: The page reports success, but the data disappears after refresh. Confirm that the backend actually wrote to the database and that refresh queries the same record. Fix the cause, then save, refresh, and inspect the database record directly.
